findings.title: Stale duplicate test file committed
findings.description: The diff adds `CoreServiceFactory.test.ts-E`, a 146-line copy of the pre-change `CoreServiceFactory.test.ts`. Its index line matches the old blob (`e6539010`), and it still calls `createContextPipeline(FIXTURE_PROJECT_PATH)` with one argument (lines 29, 35, 59, 99, 119, 141). It looks like a backup left by `sed -i -E` on macOS. Vitest's `*.test.ts` glob does not pick it up, but it is dead code that will show up in every search for the old call signature. Delete it.

findings.title: Adoption failures other than AdoptionError degrade to an error stub
findings.description: The comment at line 147 says "Errors propagate", but only `AdoptionError` is rethrown (line 123). Any other failure in the adoption step goes to the generic catch at lines 119-125 and comes back as the "⚠️ Error generating context" stub. Examples in this step: a malformed `.context-forge.toml` (`readAdoptionState` throws the parser's plain error, pinned by `adoptionState.test.ts:59-63`), or a non-ENOENT read failure in `recognizeCi` (`ciDetection.ts:49-54` rethrows it). `build.ts` prints the stub as the prompt and does not fail. `ContextIntegrator.test.ts:434` pins this behavior. Either wrap the adoption step's errors in `AdoptionError` with `cause`, or correct the comment and the test together so the stated contract matches the behavior.

findings.title: Adoption is silently skipped when project.projectPath is absent
findings.description: The resolver receives `project.projectPath`, but `ProjectData.projectPath` is optional (`types/project.ts:17`). When it is missing, the condition at line 150 is false, `adoption` is null, and the concept prompt is built for a repository that may be brownfield. No error and no notice are produced. The pipeline already knows its root, since `createContextPipeline(projectPath, ...)` takes it (`CoreServiceFactory.ts:30`, `:51`). The CLI (`build.ts:51`) and the MCP tool guard this case, so only library callers that omit `projectPath` reach it. It is still the silent fallback that the diff's own comment at line 122 warns against. Bind the root inside `createAdoptionResolver` from the pipeline's `projectPath`, or throw when eligibility is met and no path is available.

findings.title: Wrap-and-rethrow without the required ERROR log
findings.description: `persistInProgress` catches any error from `writeAdoptionState`, rethrows it as `AdoptionError` with `cause`, and logs nothing. The project's exception rule (CLAUDE.md, "Exception Handling" (a)) requires ERROR-level logging before a re-raise. Core has no logger, so `console.error`, as used at `ContextIntegrator.ts:124`, is the nearest convention. Add that log before the throw.

findings.title: Default instruction repeated a fourth time
findings.description: The diff adds `project.instruction || 'implementation'` alongside the existing copies at lines 216, 244 and 289. Compute it once in `generateWithTemplateEngine` and pass it on, and define the default in one constant.

findings.title: Parity test's CLI half re-implements build.ts instead of running it
findings.description: The "CLI path" copies the wiring from `build.ts` (override, then `createContextPipeline`, then `generateContextFromProject`). It does not call `build.ts`. The `persist` argument is guarded separately by `build.test.ts:227`, but other changes to the CLI path would not be caught. Say so in the test header, or move the shared step into a helper that both paths call.

findings.title: Remedy text and state literal repeated
findings.description: `DECLINE_REMEDY` repeats the sentence in `adoptionFacts.ts:93` (with backticks). The literal `'in_progress'` appears at lines 88 and 107, while `ADOPTION_STATES` in `ConfigKeys.ts:28` is the single source. Define the remedy once and reference the state constant.

findings.title: ContextIntegrator.ts exceeds the file-size guideline
findings.description: The file is 397 lines against the ~300-line guideline, and this diff adds about 20 of them. Not blocking, but the next change to this file should extract the adoption wiring.

findings.title: Comment overstates the import boundary
findings.description: The comment says the rule "keeps services/ and adoption/ from importing each other's internals". It does not. `adoption/adoptionResolver.ts:13-15` imports `services/` internals, and `CoreServiceFactory.ts:12` imports `adoption/adoptionResolver.js` directly. The review doc (`project-documents/user/reviews/261-review.slice.detection-and-adoption-state.md:101`) accepted the two-way dependency. Narrow the comment to what is enforced: the integrator imports `contracts.ts` only.

findings.title: Step helpers are awaited correctly and the outcome switches are exhaustive
findings.description: I checked the callee signatures. `presentPaths` (`presentPaths.ts:31`) and `recognizeCi` (`ciDetection.ts:73`) are synchronous, and they are called without `await`, which is correct. `readHistory`, `findPlanningArtifacts` and `measureSourceVolume` are async and awaited. `isSelected` and the renderer's `describeOutcome` have `never` default branches, and `NOT_EVALUATED` carries the `not-evaluated` kind.

findings.title: Guide check runs before any state write
findings.description: `assertGuideSupportsAdoption` runs before `persistInProgress`, so a guide without the profile or prompt leaves `adoption.state` unset. `adoptionResolver.test.ts` covers this with "rejects a guide without the profile, before writing". The remedy `cf build --it` in the persist-failure message matches the flag defined at `build.ts:36`.
